blocks.text: Guru Gobind Singh is presented as concluding that the Panth had to be fashioned for open struggle, because sovereignty would never come without war and the sacrifice of Guru Tegh Bahadur had already made peace with Mughal domination impossible. (9–11)
The empire is described as an old tree whose roots were already rotten; now, the Guru thought, the time had come to strike with the sword and bring its fall to completion. (12–13)

Yet he did not desire kingship for himself. Instead he began to think about lifting up others, raising the lowly, and creating a new martial order answerable to the house of Nanak rather than to worldly rulers. (14–16)
